body: Historical data indicates Warren Buffett has blunt message on stock market for 2026. Stock Market Week in Review – 04/27. Trump hails stock

The S&P 500 enters is weakest seasonality stretch of the year. **Good morning, investors.** It doesn’t feel like it, but the S&P 500 has gained almost 28% over the last 12 months, geopolitical uncertainty and all. A red-hot S&P 500 doesn’t squash the “sell in May” cliche that follows markets every year. May is the fourth-weakest month of the year historically, and it also kicks off a stretch of seasonality so middling that it’s earned itself a moniker. **In nine of the past 10 years** stocks have gained during this stretch, and 2025 brought the strongest “sell in May” cycle on record, according to Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist for Carson. As *Opening Bell Daily* has documented, stocks continue to smash records despite the Iran conflict, elevated oil prices, rising inflation fears and a changing of the guard at the Federal Reserve. * Positive in May 12 of the last 13 years.

But S&P 500 (^GSPC) history shows the seasonal map has changed a lot depending on the market era — and the modern version looks much less friendly to the slogan. From 1928 to 1941 — the eve of the Great Depression through the early part of World War II — the stretch from May through August was actually the strongest part of the year, according to Yahoo Finance data. From 1960 through 1987 — a period that included the inflation shocks of the 1970s, Volcker-era rate hikes, and the 1987 crash — the S&P 500’s May through August return was barely positive, making the middle of the year look like dead money compared with the rest of the calendar. And in years when the S&P 500 was up more than 5% through April — as it was this year — the rest of the year finished higher 23 of the past 25 times.
